candidates.title: Susan Gough's psychological operations role as a source for the WSJ article
candidates.place_text: Booz Allen Hamilton / Department of Defense, USA
candidates.quote: One of the articles primary sources is Susan Gough, whose own LinkedIn, along with independent sources, confirms her lead role in Booz Allen Hamilton's Psychological Operations Consulting Practice for the Department of Defense.
documents: The Pentagon Disinformation That Fueled America's UFO Mythology (The Wall Street Journal)

link.reason: This is about Susan Gough's psychological operations role at Booz Allen as a source for the WSJ article. The Gough stories in the corpus cover other moments: George Mason, the non-human intelligence statement and Gimbal.

candidates.title: Malmstrom 1967: guards report a red glowing object at the front gate
candidates.quote: On March 24th, 1967, Robert Salas, a first lieutenant stationed at Malmstrom Air Force Base, said he received a call from top side guards saying that they had seen strange lights in the sky making odd maneuvers.

link.reason: Both are the March 1967 Malmstrom encounter, where guards reported a red glowing object and Salas's missiles were disabled.
link.difference: Gives the date as March 24, 1967 and centres on the guards' call about lights moving oddly, credited to Salas, Jamieson and Larry King.

candidates.title: Salas: all 10 missiles went off alert
candidates.quote: All 10 missiles were off alert. All 10. Whole flight was off alert. All red.

link.reason: This is the same Malmstrom shutdown, where all 10 missiles went off alert. A corpus telling uses the same words.
link.difference: Told firsthand by Salas, where the matching corpus quote is credited to Bob Jameson.

candidates.title: Robert Hastings' record of 167 nuclear base witnesses
candidates.quote: His name is Robert Hastings, and he is the authoritative chronicler of 167 Q-cleared nuclear base employees that have all witnessed UFOs.

link.reason: Both are Hastings' record of 167 nuclear base witnesses in UFOs and Nukes.
link.difference: Describes the witnesses as Q-cleared.

candidates.title: Teenage Hastings shown radar tracking unknowns at Malmstrom
candidates.quote: In high school, Hastings worked as a janitor there, and a radar operator who took young Hastings under his wing called the 16-year-old over to show him that the base was actually tracking what they called unknowns at the time.

link.reason: Both are teenage Hastings, working as a janitor at Malmstrom, being called over by a radar operator to see unknowns.
link.difference: Gives his age as 16 and calls the man a radar operator.

candidates.title: Hastings sees five blips on the radar scope
candidates.quote: I saw five blips in the sort of northeast quadrant of his radar scope.

link.reason: This is Hastings' own account of seeing five blips on the Malmstrom radar scope.
link.difference: No difference; a corpus telling already has this quote.

candidates.title: Montana truck driver and police officer see the UFO
candidates.place_text: near Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana
candidates.quote: A local truck driver in Montana and police officer are also on record having seen the UFO in the area.

link.reason: Both are the 1967 sighting by a local truck driver near Malmstrom, told elsewhere as the Belt truck driver.
link.difference: Adds a police officer as a second witness and leaves out the light landing in a ravine.

candidates.title: John Mills' 1993 sighting and the base being swarmed
candidates.quote: In 1993, a missile technician named John Mills stationed at Malmstrom also saw UFOs on his way back to the base. When he returned, officers there said the base had been swarmed.

link.reason: Both are John Mills' January 1993 sighting while driving back to Malmstrom.
link.difference: Adds that officers said the base had been swarmed when he got back.

candidates.title: Forest service worker sees a huge elliptical saucer near Malmstrom
candidates.place_text: campground near Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana
candidates.quote: On the UFO thing, I was working for the forest service, not too far from Malmstrom Air Force Base. One day I was up there in a forest service pickup truck at a certain campground, and I was there and suddenly I look up and I would I say suddenly it was just in the sky.

link.reason: Both are the forest service worker's sighting near Malmstrom, which the corpus credits to Chris Langan.
link.difference: The speaker is not named here, and the object is described as a huge elliptical saucer.

candidates.title: WSJ claim that Malmstrom was a secret EMP experiment
candidates.quote: So anyways, this Wall Street Journal reporter named Joel Schechtman writes that this was all a secret EMP or electromagnetic pulse experiment, seeing if the US could shut down our own nukes with people present as if that's not incredibly dangerous and reckless and has any precedent.
documents: The Pentagon Disinformation That Fueled America's UFO Mythology (The Wall Street Journal)

link.reason: Both are the WSJ claim that the 1967 Malmstrom shutdown was a secret EMP experiment, in Schechtman's article.
link.difference: Adds that the host called it dangerous, reckless and without precedent.

candidates.title: SAC documents show puzzlement and a Boeing investigation
candidates.quote: There's even documentation from Malmstrom's strategic air command itself, saying that they were extremely puzzled around the event and that they had no idea what was going on.
documents: Strategic Air Command documentation on Malmstrom

link.reason: Both tell of the 1967 Echo Flight/Malmstrom SAC documentation and Boeing's investigation into the shutdown.
link.difference: Stresses that SAC documents say the command was extremely puzzled and had no idea what happened.

candidates.title: Salas rebuts the EMP explanation
candidates.quote: Bob Salas responded to this claim, quote unquote, it would have been irresponsible and unthinkable for the U.S. Air Force to jeopardize the operational status of these weapons.

link.reason: Salas's rebuttal disputes the WSJ claim that an EMP test caused the 1967 Malmstrom shutdowns; it is a competing account of the same event.
link.difference: Salas argues the Air Force would never have risked the weapons' operational status with an EMP test, which contradicts the WSJ explanation.

candidates.title: WSJ claim that Air Force hazing rituals explain UFO mythology
candidates.quote: Okay, and then you have this second claim that the article makes, that Air Force hazing rituals explain widespread UFO mythology.
documents: The Pentagon Disinformation That Fueled America's UFO Mythology (The Wall Street Journal)

link.reason: The hazing-ritual claim is a separate thesis in the WSJ article; the nearest story covers only the article's EMP explanation for Malmstrom.

candidates.title: 1949 emergency meeting on UFOs and nukes at Killeen base
candidates.quote: Can someone please, for the love of God, explain documents from the Air Force dating back to 1949 discussing an emergency meeting around UFOs and nukes, taking place at Killeen base camps with the Army CIC, FBI, Office of Naval Intelligence and CIA present?

link.reason: The same 1949 emergency meeting at Killeen Base, Texas, about UFOs near the nuclear stockpile.
link.difference: Lists Army CIC, FBI, ONI and CIA as present at the meeting.

candidates.title: FBI document on the UFO-nuclear connection
candidates.quote: This FBI document discussing the same UFO and nuclear connection,

link.reason: The 1949 FBI document on UFOs and nuclear sites matches the 1949 FBI memo to Hoover about discs and balls of fire around Los Alamos.
link.difference: Gives no content beyond the UFO-nuclear connection and does not name Hoover.

candidates.title: General Twining says UFOs are not visionary or fictitious
candidates.quote: or in 1947, General Nathan Twining, responsible for all aircraft development in the Air Force at the time, saying that UFOs are not visionary or fictitious.

link.reason: The same 1947 Twining memo saying UFOs are neither visionary nor fictitious.

candidates.title: Japanese town near Fukushima obsessed with UFOs
candidates.quote: Tell me how debunking one nuclear UFO-related case in 1967 explains a town in Japan, next to their nuclear civilian grid in Fukushima, where the residents have frequent sightings and are obsessed with UFOs,

link.reason: The same UFO-obsessed Japanese town next to the Fukushima nuclear grid.
link.difference: Does not name the town or give dates.

candidates.title: Bariloche 1995: pilot can't land and is chased by a UFO
candidates.quote: or at Bariloche, Argentina, next to their civilian grid, where a commercial pilot in 1995 literally couldn't land the plane due to an outage and a UFO chasing his plane.

link.reason: The same 1995 Bariloche, Argentina case with a commercial plane near the civilian nuclear grid.
link.difference: Adds that the pilot could not land because of an outage and that a UFO chased the plane.

candidates.title: Bob Jacobs' 1964 Vandenberg sighting and denial he worked there
candidates.quote: What about Bob Jacobs' sighting in 1964 at Vandenberg, where he was removed as a government employee despite having managed over 130 people? They denied that he ever worked there until later, his superior, Major Mansmen, admitted that he did work there a couple decades later.

link.reason: Centres on the Air Force denying that Bob Jacobs worked at Vandenberg after his 1964 sighting, which is the records-denied story.
link.difference: Adds that he managed over 130 people and that Major Mansmann later admitted Jacobs worked there; leaves out the mailbox threat.

candidates.title: Jacobs' officer efficiency reports
candidates.quote: My officer efficiency reports are in there.

link.reason: Jacobs cites his officer efficiency reports as proof against the denial that he served at Vandenberg, which is the same records-denial story.
link.difference: Told firsthand by Jacobs, citing his officer efficiency reports as evidence.

candidates.title: Host has seen Jacobs' DD214
candidates.quote: By the way, I've seen Bob Jacobs' DD214. He definitely worked at Vandenberg.

link.reason: The host says he has personally seen Bob Jacobs' DD214, which shows Jacobs served at Vandenberg. The nearest DD214 story is about Charles Hall's records, a different person, and the Jacobs records story is about the Air Force denying his service, not the host seeing the document.

candidates.title: Jacobs harassed: mailbox blown up and threatening call
candidates.quote: In Jacob's case, they blew up his mailbox and fucked with him endlessly.

link.reason: Same story: Bob Jacobs was harassed after the 1964 Vandenberg events, including his mailbox being blown up.
link.difference: Mentions only the mailbox and 'endless' harassment; leaves out the denied records and the threatening phone call.

candidates.title: Grusch reprisals at the NGA
candidates.quote: David Grusch, who experienced serious reprisals while in government and was dragged through the mud at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, should receive a large check in the mail.

link.reason: Both are about the reprisals David Grusch says he suffered in government, but this telling puts them at the NGA, where the story puts the harasser at the NRO.
link.difference: Places the reprisals at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency instead of the National Reconnaissance Office, and does not mention the medical file leak.

candidates.title: Karl Nell's op-ed co-authored by a former cabinet member, refused by WSJ
candidates.quote: Last year, my friend Karl Nell, army representative of the UAP task force, who helped spearhead many of the army's most important tech modernization efforts, wrote an op-ed intended for The Wall Street Journal.
documents: emails between Karl Nell and The Wall Street Journal

link.reason: Same story: the op-ed Karl Nell co-wrote with a former cabinet member, which the Wall Street Journal did not publish.
link.difference: Dates it to 2024 ('last year'), names Nell as the Army's UAP task force representative, cites emails with the WSJ and credits Kurt McConnell.

candidates.title: Host meets WSJ opinion editor Lena Bell
candidates.place_text: The Wall Street Journal headquarters, New York
candidates.quote: I even met her in person at The Wall Street Journal headquarters.

link.reason: The host's in-person visit to the WSJ to argue for the op-ed is the same advocacy effort the story already records ('I also went to the Wall Street Journal').
link.difference: Names the opinion editor, Lena Bell, says they met at WSJ headquarters in New York, and mentions the 'UFOs and Nukes' document.

candidates.title: David Spergel as WSJ's de facto UFO advisor
candidates.quote: Lena told me that a guy named David Spergel is their de facto advisor on UFOs, and he says that UFOs are all space trash, light reflections, and temperature inversions.

link.reason: Same story: during the WSJ op-ed effort, David Spergel was the paper's adviser on UFOs and dismissed them.
link.difference: Says Lena Bell is the source and spells out Spergel's explanation: space trash, light reflections and temperature inversions.

candidates.title: Menzel: the objects are not unidentified
candidates.quote: First of all, the objects are not unidentified. We know what they are.

link.reason: This is Menzel's own debunking claim that UFOs are already identified. The nearest Menzel stories are about his clearances and the destroyed plates, not this claim.

candidates.title: Menzel's high clearances
candidates.quote: Menzel happened to hold extremely high clearances at the NSA, CIA, and Navy.

link.reason: Same claim: Donald Menzel held very high clearances at the NSA, CIA and Navy.
link.difference: Leaves out JFK and the claim that Menzel admitted the clearances to him.

candidates.title: Menzel caught destroying astronomical records
candidates.quote: He was also caught destroying astronomical records by fellow astronomer Dorrit Hoffleit, as she documents in her biography.

link.reason: Same story: Dorrit Hoffleit caught Donald Menzel destroying astronomical plates or records at Harvard.
link.difference: Names Hoffleit's biography as the document where she records it.

candidates.title: Menzel stops the Harvard sky survey in 1953
candidates.quote: In 1953, Donald Menzel also stopped the astronomers at Harvard to carry out their very famous sky survey where they were monitoring the entire sky.

link.reason: Menzel halting the Harvard sky survey in 1953 is a separate event from his destroying plates. None of the stories is about the survey being stopped.

candidates.title: Spergel of the Simons Foundation chairs the NASA UAP working group
candidates.quote: The head of the Simons Foundation, guy named Dr. David Spergel. He was tapped to be the chair of the NASA UAP working group.

link.reason: Both say David Spergel, head of Jim Simons' foundation, was chosen to chair NASA's UAP working group in 2022-2023.

candidates.title: Weinstein speculates the Simons Foundation hides a secret physics program
candidates.quote: Yeah, Weinstein is is on Rogan actively speculating that this is housing a sort of secret physics program involving all the top differential geometers in the US.

link.reason: The quote is the same as the story's: Weinstein on Rogan guessing that a Simons-linked body houses a secret physics program built around top differential geometers.
link.difference: The telling's title puts the speculated program at the Simons Foundation, where the story names Renaissance Technologies.

candidates.title: Kirkpatrick lobbied against the UAP Disclosure Act
candidates.quote: And hopefully, when the UAP Disclosure Act goes up for vote again, Sean Kirkpatrick won't lobby against it like he did last time.

link.reason: The claim that Kirkpatrick lobbied against the UAP Disclosure Act is a distinct claim. The nearest story is the wider push to pass the Act in the NDAA, which does not mention Kirkpatrick's opposition.
